permitDetails.rightOfEntryClause: The Illinois EPA shall be allowed to enter the Permittee's property where actual or potential effluent, emission or noise sources are located or where any activity is to be conducted pursuant to this permit; to have access to and to copy any records required to be kept under the terms and conditions of this permit; to inspect, including during any hours of operation of equipment constructed or operated under this permit, such equipment ...
permitDetails.extractionNotes: Document contains both 'Application No.: 08010054' and 'I.D. No.: 031440ANI'. Selected I.D. No. '031440ANI' as the primary permit identifier. Permit text contains inconsistent unit counts (document lists Fifteen (15) + Four (4) units but also refers to 'eighteen Emergency Generator Sets' and refers to 'all fourteen' in one combined-hours limit). Make and model for gensets not specified in permit.

generatorSets.referenceNumber: EGA1, EGA2, EGAR, EGA3, EGA4, EGB1, EGB2, EGBR, EGB3, EGB4, EGC1, EGC2, EGCR, EGSS, and EGSN
generatorSets.primaryFuelType: distillate fuel oil (Grades No. 1 and 2 (i.e., diesel))
generatorSets.fuelChangePermitTrigger: The use of any other fuel in any of the eighteen Emergency Generator Sets at this source requires that the Permittee first obtain a construction permit from the Illinois EPA and then perform stack testing to verify compliance with all applicable requirements.
generatorSets.operatingHoursPerUnitRollingWindow: running 12 month total (sum of current month plus preceding 11 months)
generatorSets.operatingHoursCombinedGroupRef: all fourteen 2,500 kW (3,634 HP) Diesel-Powered Emergency Generator Sets
generatorSets.allowedOperatingModes: In order for the engine to be considered an emergency stationary ICE under 40 CFR 60 Subpart IIII, any operation other than emergency operation, maintenance and testing, emergency demand response, and operation in non-emergency situations for 50 hours per year, as described in 40 CFR 60.4211(f)(1) through (3), is prohibited. Emergency engines may be operated for maintenance checks and readiness testing and may be operated up to 100 hours/year for maintenance and testing/emergency demand response subject to recordkeeping; up to 50 hours/year for non-emergency situations (counts toward the 100 hours).
generatorSets.observationFrequency: Initial compliance opacity observations: minimum total time of observations shall be 3 hours (30 6-minute averages)
